definition.question: How severed are diplomatic and crisis-management channels between Russia and NATO/EU states?
definition.low_end: Regular diplomatic and military-to-military communication functions, including hotlines, embassies and arms-control or risk-reduction dialogue.
definition.high_end: Complete severance of diplomatic relations and crisis communication channels with no hotlines or forums to manage incidents.

readings.rationale: No graded claims provided to assess. Unassessed - research needed on embassy operations, expulsions, hotline functionality and public deterrence signalling. Would be higher with mass expulsions, channel closures or explicit threats to cut ties; lower with evidence of sustained dialogue and incident-management contacts.

First assessed reading; prior 2026-10-01 was unassessed. Evidence shows significant strain but not complete severance: mass expulsions of ~400 officers in 2022 rising to ~750 by Oct 2024, plus consulate closures (Poland closed Kraków May 2025, Germany closed Bonn 18 Sep 2026 and terminated Russia House lease, summoned ambassador). Counterbalanced by functioning crisis-management: Poland invoked…

Closest to 62 on 2026-10-01. New evidence shows no additional mass expulsions, embassy/consulate closures or hotline failures beyond the 2022-2026 strain already priced in. Putin Valdai remarks and UNGA activity indicate deterrence signalling within still-functioning diplomatic forums, and Sept airspace scrambles were managed without diplomatic rupture. No move.
